questions.question: Why does the greedy approach sometimes fail in the coin change problem?

answers.a: Because it does not consider future consequences of current choices
answers.b: Because it always selects the smallest coin first
answers.c: Because it explores all possible combinations
answers.d: Because it uses too much memory

explanations.a: Correct. Greedy algorithms make decisions based only on the current step, which may lead to suboptimal global solutions.
explanations.b: Greedy usually selects the largest coin, not the smallest.
explanations.c: Exploring all combinations is characteristic of brute-force or dynamic programming, not greedy.
explanations.d: Greedy algorithms are memory efficient compared to dynamic programming.

questions.question: Which coin denomination set is a known example where the greedy approach fails?

explanations.a: Greedy works correctly for standard US coin denominations.
explanations.b: This denomination set does not produce a greedy failure case.
explanations.c: Correct. For amount 6, greedy gives 4+1+1, while optimal is 3+3.
explanations.d: Greedy works optimally for this set in most cases.

questions.question: How does dynamic programming ensure an optimal solution for the coin change problem?

answers.a: By selecting the largest denomination first
answers.b: By storing and reusing solutions to subproblems
answers.d: By reducing the number of denominations

explanations.a: Selecting the largest denomination is a greedy strategy.
explanations.b: Correct. Dynamic programming builds solutions from smaller subproblems and guarantees optimality.
explanations.c: Random choices do not ensure correctness.
explanations.d: Reducing denominations does not solve the optimization problem.

questions.question: What key difference between greedy and dynamic programming is demonstrated through the simulation?

answers.a: Greedy always uses recursion, while DP does not
answers.b: Greedy focuses on local optimization, while DP focuses on global optimization
answers.c: DP is faster in all cases
answers.d: Greedy uses more memory than DP

explanations.a: Neither greedy nor DP necessarily requires recursion.
explanations.b: Correct. Greedy optimizes locally, while dynamic programming ensures a globally optimal solution.
explanations.c: DP is not always faster due to higher time complexity.
explanations.d: Dynamic programming generally uses more memory than greedy.

questions.question: Based on the simulation results, when should dynamic programming be preferred over the greedy approach?

answers.a: When the coin denominations are canonical
answers.b: When speed is the only requirement
answers.c: When correctness and optimality are critical
answers.d: When memory usage must be minimal

explanations.a: Canonical coin systems often work well with greedy algorithms.
explanations.b: Greedy is generally faster than DP.
explanations.c: Correct. Dynamic programming guarantees optimal results even when greedy fails.
explanations.d: DP uses more memory, so it is not ideal when memory is limited.
